decision.author: gemini-antigravity
decision.rationale: R4 now explicitly enforces final displacement and history consistency, post-update KKT compliance, and physical checkpoint gates, with meaningful failure-path tests. However, the supplied full driver contains critical regressions outside the isolated acceptance method. In load(), all four Gauss-point history values for each element are populated from the same CSV column r[1], whereas R3 reads the separate history columns r[4+g]. This destroys the required 61,008-point transferred history state. In _deck(), R4 iterates using 'for name, lines in split_keyword_blocks(self.template)', although the predecessor driver treats split_keyword_blocks output as strings. This incompatible unpacking risks failure before any Abaqus subproblem. The replacement _deck() also emits nodal displacement/damage records under *INITIAL CONDITIONS, TYPE=SOLUTION rather than preserving the predecessor's element-level solution-state formatting, potentially invalidating Abaqus UEL initialization. Finally, runner() invokes the extractor with '--role', whereas the previously supplied working driver uses '--physical-nodes', '--physical-elements', and '--step'; compatibility has not been demonstrated. These defects are not covered by the 11 reported tests, which exercise acceptance gates or static package checks rather than real deck construction, data round-tripping and extractor invocation. Preserve R4's corrected acceptance logic, restore verified R3-compatible history loading, deck construction and extractor contracts, and add integration tests verifying all four independent Gauss-point histories, generated mechanical/phase decks, and extractor CLI compatibility. Independently re-review a new hash-bound corrected candidate. Do not submit R4. Approval would concern execution qualification only, never automatic physical acceptance.
